title: Patient perspective on treatment with monoclonal antibody in the memory clinic: Treatment expectations, experiences and outcomes
summary: Monoclonal antibody therapies aim to slow disease progression in early Alzheimer’s disease. Treatment involves repeated appointments, infusions and monitoring, and may be accompanied by side effects. PATH-MAKER examines patients’ expectations before treatment initiation and their satisfaction, psychological distress and treatment experiences over the following 18 months. Participating family members or caregivers (informants) provide additional information about their own experiences and the patient’s everyday functioning.
conditions: Informants of patients who are reciving a monoclonal antibody therapy in the memory clinic

interventions.name: Patients at the UKE Alzheimer Therapy Outpatient Clinic/Memory Clinic receiving monoclonal anti-amyloid antibody therapy. Participation follows an informational discussion in which all details of the study are communicated, and signed informed consent is obtained.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients: Treatment with monoclonal anti-amyloid antibodies at UKE ATA/Memory Clinic; participation after information and obtained informed consent; ability to complete questionnaires; sufficient cognitive functioning; Cognitive testing (Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer’s Disease [CERAD]) in the past 6 months

Informants: Family members, friends, partners or caregivers of participating patients; voluntary participation after receiving study information and obtained informed consent; ability to complete questionnaires; sufficient cognitive functioning.
Exclusion criteria:
none
